messages.subject: Temporal models within groups
parts:
I have seen discussion of temporal models when the structure applies to the outcome variable as a whole, but often the relevance of the temporal effect is how members of a group change over that time period.

 

Consider 100 subjects measured over 20 consecutive time periods. If the performance of the subject is of primary interest, we care about how each subject’s performance changes over time, not so much how the population’s performance changes over time as a whole (although that may be worth accounting for as well if there is a true shared effect). We want to know not only who performs well or who performs poorly, but how they are trending over time and, if we forecasted, how they would be expected to perform in time periods 21 through 25 given the trend observed as they approached time period 20. Notably, periods 21 through 25 will not have been seen before so ideally the data structure needs to be willing to accept “new” levels of time period while still benefitting from the trend up through time period 20.

 

Consider this as a gaussian model with subject levels 1 through 100 and time periods 1 through 20.

 

This sort of temporal structure seems like a potentially unique area of strength for INLA. Some latent model options might include:

 

  • “iid” models, particularly for ease of modeling:
  1. f(subject, model=”iid”) + f(time, model=”iid”)
  2. f(time, subject, model=”iid”)
  3. f(time, replicate=subject, model=”iid”) [
  4. f(time, group=subject, model=”iid”)

 

  • some of the above instead using “ar1,” “rw1” or “rw2”, particularly if we want to effectively forecast on unseen time periods rather than just predict on some average of the past.

 

  • some sort of state-space model (like that from Virgilio’s helpful book) incorporating a variant of the above.

 

Or perhaps the more intuitive approach here is to view the structures as f(subject, time) rather than the other way around. (Probably not, but it’s not always intuitive why a model structure is ordered the way that it is).

 

Can you shed some light on the best latent structure candidates for a model like this? Thank you.

               

Jonathan
